doc.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23

title: Starting on piano, banjo and playing in bands
summary: Asked about piano, he says he started on it, read music for Dixieland bands, played for money on banjo from youth, and never played solo alone.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Didn't, I'll say that you played a little piano?
Well, yeah, I started on piano. You did? Yeah.
What sort of a style did you, what style of piano did you play back then?
Well, you had to play something like Dixieland with them. But they had to have somebody read the music. Yeah. And read it out to them. At that time they were very slow readers.
And you could read it? Yeah. My mother's children. Oh yeah. My mother.
I had to take piano lessons, you know, when I was a kid. Oh yeah. Yeah. So did you play in barrel houses and at fish fries?

No. I used to play for parties and things like that with Red Al and things like that. But most of the week when I played it was for money. Yeah. Even when I was young, you know, I went out there and played for money, banjo. Oh yeah. When the guitar was a banjo then.
But in bands or also solo? In bands?
No, I mean in bands or solo? In bands. You never played solo?

No, not by myself, no. Yeah. But I played solo with the solo written out or solo, you know, they give me in the band. I had to play a whole lot of solos playing with Joe Liggins, you know. Yeah. But we only had six pieces. Oh.
